memory_update.text: DPZ should remain the reference benchmark for franchisor-controlled dough manufacturing and distribution economics within the Restaurants theme.
PFGC is a plausible underfollowed outsourced procurement and distribution proxy for restaurant chains and independents lacking internal franchisor supply-chain scale.
LW maps to the ingredient-manufacturing side of the node; its QSR customer concentration and product consistency requirements make it relevant to restaurant system dependency analysis.

FARM is a speculative micro-cap shadow candidate for restaurant beverage/DSD supply-chain exposure; survival into later layers requires proof of recurring restaurant-chain or franchise-system revenue.

Layer 1C should search for smaller public commissary, bakery, sauce, protein, packaging, equipment-service, and route-density suppliers that disclose franchise or multi-unit restaurant customer relationships.

node: Franchisor-controlled procurement, dough/ingredient manufacturing, and distribution systems
summary: Layer 1B expansion found one reference leader that directly embodies the node, Domino's, and three public-market discovery candidates that map to outsourced or ingredient-level equivalents: Performance Food Group as a chain/independent restaurant distribution platform, Lamb Weston as a high-dependency prepared ingredient supplier to major QSR systems, and Farmer Bros. as a speculative micro-cap coffee/tea DSD supplier to foodservice customers. The core Serenity question for later layers is whether economics accrue to integrated franchisors themselves or to third-party suppliers that smaller restaurant systems rely on because they lack Domino's-style procurement, manufacturing, and distribution scale.
